question.text:
consider the following grammar given below:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S \rightarrow A a B \mid \epsilon \\
& A \rightarrow b S B \mid \epsilon \\
& B \rightarrow A b \mid B
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text { A. } \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{A})=\{b, \epsilon\}, \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{A})=\{a, b\}, \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b, \epsilon\}, \\
& \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b, \S\} \\\\
& \text { B. } \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{A})=\{b, \epsilon\}, \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{A})=\{a, b\}, \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{B})=\{b\}, \\
& \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b, \S\} \\\\
& \text { C. } \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{A})=\{b, \epsilon\}, \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{A})=\{a, b, \$\}, \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b, \epsilon\}, \\
& \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b, \S\} \\\\
& \text { D. } \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{A})=\{b, \epsilon\}, \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{A})=\{a, b, \$\}, \mathbf{F I R S T}(\mathbf{B})=\{b\}, \\
& \mathbf{F O L L O W}(\mathbf{B})=\{a, b\}
\end{aligned}
$$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following Grammar $G$, with $A$ as the start symbol. The grammar $G$ has three incomplete productions denoted by (1), (2), and (3).

$$
\begin{aligned}
& A \rightarrow r B T \mid(1) \\
& B \rightarrow p A S \mid(2) \\& S \rightarrow t \\
& T \rightarrow(3) \mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$


The set of terminals is $\{p, q, r, s, t\}$. The FIRST and FOLLOW sets of the different non-terminals are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{FIRST}(A)=\{r, p\} \\
& \operatorname{FIRST}(B)=\{p, \epsilon\} \\
& \operatorname{FIRST}(T)=\{q, \epsilon\} \\
& \operatorname{FOLLOW}(A)=\{t, \$\} \\
& \operatorname{FOLLOW}(B)=\{t,q, \$\}\\
& \operatorname{FOLLOW}(T)=\{t, \$\}
\end{aligned}
$$


Which of the following options correctly fills in the incomplete information?(select all that apply)

  1. (1) $A \rightarrow p C$ (2) $B \rightarrow \epsilon$ (3) $T \rightarrow q$
     
  2. (1) $A \rightarrow p C$ (2) $B \rightarrow t$ (3) $T \rightarrow q B$
     
  3. (1) $A \rightarrow p S$ (2) $B \rightarrow \epsilon$ (3) $T \rightarrow q$
     
  4. (1) $A \rightarrow p t$ (2) $B \rightarrow \epsilon$ (3) $T \rightarrow q B$
question.subject: Compiler Design
